notes: Still unfilled, but for a much narrower reason than when this record was first written, and the narrowing is the useful part. Oregon's fee-making machinery has now been read end to end and it authorises nothing for speed. ORS 56.140, Fees; waiver; rules, is a closed list - $100 for each formation document including articles of organization delivered for filing under ORS 63.051, $100 for annual reports, $275 for foreign registrations, $50 for any other business registry document, $20 for service of process - and its rulemaking power reaches only copying and certifying records and, in a later subsection, computer lists and terminal access. ORS chapter 63 has no fee section at all. The open question that left was whether a rule had added what the statute does not authorise, and it has not: the Corporation Division's own administrative rules, OAR chapter 160 division 5, headed FEES AND REFUNDS, are four rules and they price public records, certified and regular copies, certificates of existence and of record, decorative certificates, customised database searches, research at $50 per hour, notarial acts by division employees, and the refund of overpayments. There is no charge for filing anything faster. Division 10, the Business Registry Section rules, was read as well; its single occurrence of the word is a definition in an unrelated rule about the state licensing directory, which excludes 'non-normative fees, such as late fee or expedite fee' from what agencies must report about licences, and says nothing about what this division sells. What has changed on the network is worth recording precisely, because the earlier reading of it was too pessimistic. The Business Registry host is not unreadable - it answers a scripted client with a JavaScript challenge, and a real browser completes that challenge by itself and gets the site. That is how the administrative rules above were read, and it also opened the Oregon Business Registry, the division's actual filing application: its public surface offers no expedited option, and the eleven scripts its landing page loads contain no occurrence of the word at all. That is a weaker instrument than it looks, though, because the filing flow itself is behind an account and is server-rendered rather than delivered as one bundle, so the absence covers the front door and not the checkout. The division's own web host is the half that has not moved. It resolves to two public addresses that both resolvers agree on, and it accepts no TCP connection on 443 or 80 with the connection routed either way - dead everywhere rather than route-dependent, measured again today. Between them, the fee schedule, the Articles of Organization form and its instructions, the division's help page and its FAQ all sit there, and the Business Registry's own footer links point straight into them. So the record still does not say no. The standing counterexample in this namespace is a state whose only charge for speed exists as agency practice, appears in no statute and no rule, and is printed on the office's own form packet - and Oregon's form packets are exactly the documents that cannot be opened.
needsReview: Every expedite field and every standard-processing field. What is left is narrow and it is all on one host, sos.oregon.gov, which makes no TCP connection on either route: (1) the Corporation Division fee schedule under business/Documents/business-registry-forms/, for any expedited line the statute and the rules do not carry; (2) the Articles of Organization form and its instructions, the document class where an unstatutory same-day charge has turned up in another state; (3) the division's corporation-division-help page and its business FAQ, which are the only places Oregon would state a processing time - nothing reachable in this session states one, which is why isPublished is null rather than false. Also unread and unreadable without an account: the Oregon Business Registry checkout, where a fee presented only at payment would appear. Do not spend another session probing the dead host itself; it has now been measured on both routes twice.

No charge for expedited filing of any document

OAR chapter 160, division 10, BUSINESS REGISTRY SECTION - consulted in full; its only occurrence of the word is a definition excluding late and expedite fees from what agencies report to the state licensing directory, which is not a Corporation Division filing charge
